assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration-corrected electron optics is a textbook case of a new instrument that opened a door: sub-angstrom, atom-by-atom imaging and spectroscopy of interfaces, defects and nanostructures is now routine across physics, materials science and chemistry. The invention was demonstrated experimentally, not only proposed, and its impact on what can be seen and verified is lasting and very broad.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the optical theory of aberration correction, while Haider and Urban built and demonstrated the working corrector in a TEM and showed the resolution gain. This is a clean and historically well-documented three-person configuration. Other pioneers (for example the earlier Scherzer theorem tradition and the parallel STEM correction work) are outside the supplied credit, so the committee should check the record of who did the original work.
assessment.maturity: Mature: correctors have been commercial and widely used for roughly two decades, with independent confirmation worldwide and prior recognition by other major prizes. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Parallel STEM-corrector developments outside the credited names may deserve weight when settling priority; I am relying on memory of the historical record rather than independent verification.
As a microscopist I have a possible disciplinary bias and would expect colleagues to test the physics-versus-instrumentation balance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and allow tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. It is a clear, experimentally verified invention that opened new measurement regimes.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and carried out the first demonstrations. Ye's group brought the clock to its highest accuracy and stability and developed many-body and comparison techniques. A two-person prize is natural, though the committee should weigh the prior ion-clock and frequency-comb prizes when judging novelty.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with multiple independent labs reproducing and improving the performance, and international comparisons ongoing.
uncertainties: The relation to earlier frequency metrology prizes could lead some members to see this as incremental.
Whether Ye is better credited here or with other clock-related candidates is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theoretical prediction of flat bands at the magic angle was followed by the experimental observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene, creating the moire quantum materials field. The experiment demonstrated a new, tunable materials platform whose consequences continue to grow.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the original experimental discovery with the co-workers who built the devices. The supplied credit omits the experimental first author and some other contributors, so allocation within the experimental team must be checked carefully against the record.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many independent laboratories within a few years, though the interpretation of the superconducting mechanism is not yet settled. Timing is reasonable but somewhat early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism and the full phase diagram remain debated.
Credit among the experimental team (junior contributors outside the credited names) is not resolved by the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reproducible room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in 1995 was the original experiment that led to magnetic tunnel junction read heads, MRAM and spintronic sensors, with large technological impact. The later MgO coherent-tunnelling work then raised the effect by an order of magnitude.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported the original room-temperature effect, and this is the discovery I would anchor on. Parkin made the major MgO and device advances (with Yuasa and others, not credited here), which is a second, distinct step. Credit therefore splits between original discovery and later enhancement, and I would not simply give the prize to the most prominent name.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with decades of independent confirmation and deployment in hard drives and memory.
uncertainties: Whether the committee should recognise the MgO step, with Parkin, alongside the original discovery.
Overlap with the 2007 giant magnetoresistance prize could make some members view this as incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with a cubic-kilometre detector opened neutrino astronomy as a new window on the universe, with later association to a blazar and the Galactic plane. It is both an instrument achievement and a discovery.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the conception and realisation of IceCube and Spiering was a key figure in the detector's predecessors and the collaboration. Because this is a large collaboration, a prize to two individuals would need a justification that the committee can defend as identifying the people who did the original work.
assessment.maturity: The discovery has been confirmed with independent analyses, and source identification is progressing, but the origin of the diffuse flux is still largely open.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale credit and the exclusion of other leaders of IceCube and its precursors (such as AMANDA and Baikal).
Source identification is still incomplete, which may argue for waiting.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: SASE-based X-ray free-electron lasers deliver femtosecond, coherent, brilliant X-ray pulses that let people image structure and dynamics that could not be seen before. As a door-opening tool for materials, chemistry and biology, the impact is large and demonstrated by working facilities.
assessment.attribution: Credit for the SASE concept (Kondratenko and Saldin; Bonifacio, Pellegrini and Narducci), the high-gain theory and the first X-ray lasing is spread over many people and groups. The supplied three-name configuration may not fairly reflect all of them, and there is a real question about who did the original work.
assessment.maturity: Mature: several facilities have been operating for over a decade with independent confirmation and heavy scientific use.
uncertainties: Disputed and distributed attribution between theory, early proposal and the machine builders; some key people are not in the supplied credit.
The prize may be seen as recognising an accelerator technology rather than a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of the double pulsar gave a unique laboratory for strong-field gravity, with several independent relativistic effects measured to high precision and consistent with general relativity. It rests on a clear original observation followed by careful, verified follow-up.
assessment.attribution: Burgay made the original discovery in survey data with Lyne's and Kramer's teams, and Kramer led the extended timing tests. The credited three plausibly cover discovery and exploitation, and it would also bring a woman discoverer into view, which I think the committee should welcome where merit supports it.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed through long timing campaigns and consistent with other pulsar tests, though the prize logic overlaps with the 1993 binary pulsar recognition.
uncertainties: Novelty relative to the earlier Hulse-Taylor prize.
Whether discovery alone or the strong-field tests should carry the motivation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy spins in diamond at room temperature created a practical solid-state quantum sensor with nanoscale resolution, used for magnetometry, thermometry and in-cell measurements. It is a new tool that lets people see things that were previously inaccessible.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group made the original single-centre optical detection, and Jelezko and Wrachtrup demonstrated coherent control. Lukin's group contributed major later sensing and quantum-register advances, but those are a different step and are better placed with other candidates.
assessment.maturity: Broad independent confirmation and growing applications, although many applications are still maturing.
uncertainties: Distinguishing the original single-spin experiments from later sensing and quantum-network developments.
Whether the prize is premature relative to the pace of application development.
